plain_description.what: Measures how reliable the per-subject model profiles are (how well two random halves of the judged questions agree), and puts a confidence interval around it by leaving out one subject (one of 14 anchor domains) at a time. Done on the 12-model board and the merged 20-model board, using already-stored verdicts (no new judge calls).
plain_description.why: The merged board's reliability of 0.7183 just cleared the 0.70 bar, and the question was whether that is a real pass or a lucky point estimate.
plain_description.information: If the lower end of the interval clears 0.70, per-subject claims can be published as reliable; if not, they need the interval printed next to them. Result: not a clear pass. The interval is about 0.61 to 0.83, so its lower end is below 0.70 on every reading. Per-subject claims may be published only with the interval. The gain from merging boards is not distinguishable from zero. Ruled later as history rather than evidence, because it was judged on the older question pool.
